$comment: Owner-approved exceptions to the pre-migration backup requirement.
The Production database workflow normally refuses to apply anything unless
PRE_MIGRATION_BACKUP_REF names a verified restore point. Warsha cannot
currently satisfy that: docs/operations/backup-runbook.md records gap G22 —
the Supabase plan is unconfirmed, PITR availability is unconfirmed, and no
restore has ever been performed. A backup that has never been restored is
So rather than fabricate a reference, or add a reusable skip-backups switch,
each exception is bound to ONE migration by name AND by content hash, with a
reason a person wrote. Change a byte of that migration and the exception
stops applying. It cannot be pointed at a different migration, cannot be
widened to a directory, and cannot be reused for the next deployment.
G22 REMAINS OPEN. An exception here is a recorded risk decision about one
specific change; it is not evidence that Warsha can restore anything.
Adding an entry is an owner decision. It is not something a deployment
should be able to grant itself.

exceptions.reason: Owner-approved exception: additive function-only migration with no data or schema mutation of existing objects; rollback is removal of the two newly introduced functions. Production restore capability remains an open release-readiness gap (G22).
